page_title: Hacksplaining - Free Interactive Secure Coding Lessons

summary.title: Hacksplaining - Free Interactive Secure Coding Lessons
summary.one_liner: Learn secure coding by exploiting real attacks in your browser, such as SQL injection, prompt injection and XSS, and then learning the fix.
takeaways: Each lesson lets you exploit a common vulnerability in the browser, then shows how to fix it.
Lessons cover the OWASP Top 10 plus LLM threats such as prompt injection.
Lessons take roughly 15-30 minutes each and include short quizzes.
Code examples are given in Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, and more.
Individual use is free; team features such as dashboards and compliance reports are paid.
summary.summary: Hacksplaining is a free, interactive secure coding training site with 45+ lessons covering the OWASP Top 10 and emerging LLM vulnerabilities. Each lesson is 15-30 minutes and combines an in-browser exploit with vulnerable and secure code examples in languages such as Python, JavaScript, Java, and Go. Short quizzes follow each lesson and progress can be tracked with a free account. The page says lessons are expert-written by a human founder and that team features (dashboards, SSO, compliance reporting) are paid.
